attribution.note: Both occurrences are Zitron's own newsletter posts. In August 2024 he called it a prediction he had made since March and said he stood by it.

semantics.note: 'I believe' plus 'will' is an unhedged expectation, and he later called it his 'prediction', so this is a scored forecast. The implied 'unless AI proves itself' is not a real condition, since he predicted it would not. Reading three quarters from March 2024 as ending around late 2024 is faithful.

contract.note: Year-over-year revenue in the quarter ending 2024-12-31 is a reasonable test of 'savaging the revenues' at the end of the three-quarter window. A revenue lag after an apocalypse in December could argue for a later quarter. But double-digit growth contradicts any reading of 'savaging', so the result does not turn on the evaluator's choices. Amazon is missing, but two named giants suffice.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own earnings release, dated January 29, 2025. Revenue for the quarter ended December 31, 2024 was $69.6B, up 12% year over year. This is the source type the contract requires, and growth is the opposite of savaging.
Alphabet's own Q4 2024 earnings release, dated February 4, 2025, read from an archived copy. Revenue was $96.5B, up 12% year over year, which directly meets the contradiction condition.
Zitron's 2026 admission that he 'goofed' on the three-quarters claim. The speaker's own statements cannot settle the outcome, so this is context only.

output.rationale: The forecast said AI's collapse within about three quarters of March 2024 would savage the revenues of the biggest tech firms. The horizon has elapsed. Microsoft and Alphabet, both named in the post, each grew revenue 12% year over year in the quarter ending December 2024, per their own earnings releases. That meets the contradiction condition. Amazon's missing data does not change the result.
